description:
DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN SOURCE, found by the operator 2026-09-24.

The epic names artifact "Five Ways to Watch a Job" version 9 as what the work
is measured against. Re-read today. It carries DEDICATED TERMINAL TOKENS that
are dark in BOTH themes:

  light   --term-bg #0e161d  --term-fg #c8d4dc  --term-dim #6c7f8d
  dark    --term-bg #05090d  --term-fg #c8d4dc  --term-dim #5d6e7b

  .tt-tail { color: var(--term-fg); background: var(--term-bg); height: 132px; }
  .tt-tail .dim { color: var(--term-dim); }
  .tt-tailbar { color: var(--faint); background: var(--head); font: 11px mono; }

What was built uses --code-fg on --code-bg, which in the light theme is
#253039 on #f6f8fa: a CODE BLOCK, the same treatment as a tool stdout dump.
The design deliberately distinguishes the two -- .tt pre uses --code-bg and
.tt-tail uses --term-bg, in the same specimen, ten lines apart. progress.css
has no --term-* tokens at all, so the divergence was introduced when the tail
CSS was first written and survived because nobody compared.

SECOND DEFECT, same element: THE TAIL MUST SIT ON THE LAST LINE unless the
reader has scrolled up. Half-implemented in poly-pvs2: agentic-job.js pins to
the bottom when it SWAPS the slot on a poll, but nothing scrolls it on the
initial server render, so first paint shows the oldest of the last forty lines
next to a label reading "last line 4s ago".

FIX
- add --term-bg / --term-fg / --term-dim to all three token blocks in
  progress.css (bare :root, the prefers-color-scheme guard, and
  :root[data-theme="dark"]), matching the design values
- .tool-tail takes --term-fg on --term-bg
- scroll the tail to the bottom on initial load as well as on swap
notes:
ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE DESIGN SURVIVES, written down per the
repo rule rather than left to be rediscovered.

The design sets .tt-tail at font: 11.5px/1.5. This sheet has an
accessibility floor of 12px, enforced by
test_design_tokens.py::test_nothing_essential_is_below_twelve_pixels, which
was added after a 10px uppercase label slipped in (UI-4). A running builds
log is precisely the essential text that floor exists to protect, so the
rule wins and the tail is 12px.

Everything else matches the source: --term-bg / --term-fg / --term-dim at the
designs values in all three token blocks, and height 132px rather than the
max-height it had (a pane that resizes under the reader as lines arrive gives
scroll-to-bottom no stable frame).
title: The dsynth tail is a code block, not a terminal, and it opens on the oldest line

description:
FOUND IN DEPLOYMENT 2026-09-24, and it hid a whole feature.

server.py computes static_v as the sha256 of progress.css alone -- its comment
says so: "Content-hash cache-buster for progress.css". Both the CSS and the JS
tags then interpolate that one token:

  _base.html:23          progress.css?v={{ static_v }}
  agentic_job.html:176   agentic-job.js?v={{ static_v }}
  agentic_job_transcript.html:51   same

So a change to any .js file does not move the token. The URL is byte-identical,
every warm browser cache keeps the old script, and there is no error anywhere --
the server sends the new payload and the stale client ignores the parts it does
not know about.

OBSERVED: poly-pvs2 shipped a tail_html slot plus the JS that swaps it. On the
builder the producer published correctly and the tracker returned tail_html on
every poll, verified by curl. The page showed nothing, because the browser was
running agentic-job.js from before the deploy. progress.css was untouched by
that work -- the tail CSS had survived poly-paee -- so the token was unchanged.

There are 9 files in static/ (196K total), 5 of them .js. Any JS-only change
has always shipped this way.

FIX: hash the whole static directory, including each file relative path so a
rename or deletion also moves the token. One directory read at startup.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. static_v is now the sha256 of every file under static/, each
files relative path hashed alongside its bytes so a rename or deletion moves
the token too. One directory read at startup; static/ is 196K across 9 files.

Test pins it as a CONTRACT rather than by re-running the loop: the token the
app serves must equal the hash of the whole tree. Mutation-checked -- reverting
to progress.css alone fails that test, which is the bug as it shipped. Five more
cover a JS-only change, a CSS-only change, a rename, that every versioned tag
carries the token, and that the page still serves one.

WHY THE OLD TEST SUITE COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS: nothing asserted on the
tokens INPUTS, only that a token existed. The defect is invisible server-side --
correct HTML, correct payload, correct headers - and shows up only in a browser
that already has the file. That is also why poly-pvs2 passed 31 tests and still
showed nothing on the builder.
title: Static cache-buster is the CSS's hash, so a JS-only change ships invisibly

description:
Reported from a running job, 2026-09-24: the attempt number and turn show
briefly, then vanish while the job is still live and refreshing.

A contract mismatch between the fragment and its client.

api_job_activity_fragment renders every body `if rows else ""`, where
`rows` is only the rows NEWER than the client's cursor. The client does:

  if (data.nowbar_html !== undefined && barSlot)
      barSlot.innerHTML = data.nowbar_html;

An empty string passes `!== undefined`, so the first poll with nothing new
assigns "" and ERASES the bar. startElapsedClock() then has nothing to
tick. The cards survive the same poll only because their guard is
`if (data.cards_html && ...)` -- truthiness, which "" fails.

WHY IT LOOKS LIKE "A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME": rows arrive in bursts at turn
boundaries and vanish in between. A long tool emits nothing for its whole
duration -- a 41-minute dsynth build is 41 minutes of empty polls -- so the
bar disappears exactly during the wait it exists to explain.

The client's guard was written expecting the key to be OMITTED when there
is nothing new; the server sends "" instead. Fix on the server so the
deliberate clear still works: when a poll HAS rows and now_bar() returns
None (MANUAL tier, or the job just ended), "" is correct and must still
empty the slot.

Not a re-render problem: with no new rows the bar's content cannot have
changed (no new turn, no new tool), and the elapsed clock is client-side.
Omitting the key is both correct and free.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24.

The fragment now OMITS nowbar_html when no rows are new, rather than
sending "". The client's guard was already written for that contract; the
server was the half that disagreed.

Deliberately a presence check, not truthiness: on a poll that HAS rows,
now_bar() returning None (MANUAL tier, or the job just ended) must still
empty the slot, and truthiness would have kept a stale bar on screen
forever.

No client change. Hardening the JS to ignore "" as well would have broken
that deliberate clear, so the contract is stated in a comment at the
server instead -- one reader, one writer, one rule.

Nothing is lost by omitting it: with no new rows there is no new turn and
no new tool, so the bar's content cannot have changed, and the elapsed
clock runs client-side off a data attribute.

cards_html was never affected because its client guard is truthiness
(`if (data.cards_html && ...)`), which "" fails. That inconsistency is why
only the bar disappeared and the cards stayed -- matching the report.

Test: a poll at the newest cursor returns changed:false and no
nowbar_html key at all. 4210 pass.
title: The now-bar disappears on a live job: the fragment sends an empty bar when nothing is new

description:
poly-qqx9.8 put a running build's last lines inside the tool row that was
running it. As built it cannot work: the tracker resolves the log path
through worker._dsynth_log_candidates -> env_paths() -> a root-only
`dev-env path`, and the tracker is unprivileged. poly-paee removes the
wiring. This bead holds the decision about what, if anything, replaces it.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST "DO WHAT THE DIFF DOES". The diff publishes once per
attempt; the tail's whole value is sub-minute freshness during a 41-minute
build. Over the artifact channel that means the runner re-POSTing the last
~32 KiB every N seconds -- put_blob upserts on (bundle_id, relpath) and is
content-addressed, so an unchanged tail costs no new blob, but it is still
a periodic emitter inside the build wait loop, which is a change to the
loop rather than a tracker fix.

THREE OPTIONS, in the order I would consider them:
1. The runner publishes a rolling tail artifact every N seconds while a
   tailable tool runs. Honest, reuses the existing channel, and the
   dsynth_tail.read_tail windowing/offset/cap logic is reusable as the
   producer side.
2. Drop the feature. The full log already reaches the tracker as
   logs/full.log.gz when the build ENDS, and the tool row already shows
   the build running with an elapsed clock. The tail was a nicety.
3. Leave it for poly-fij, where a remote runner needs a general answer for
   streaming progress anyway, and a bespoke tail channel would be work
   thrown away.

What must NOT happen is the current state: a feature that looks built,
renders nothing, and says nothing about why.
notes:
SEQUENCED AFTER poly-fij.4, 2026-09-24. Not frozen for lack of a mechanism
any more -- frozen because the mechanism needs a channel that does not exist
yet.

THE TIMER PROBLEM IS SOLVED, and option 1's cost estimate above was wrong.
It said a periodic emitter would mean a background thread or a Popen rewrite
of the build path. The runner ALREADY has one: _heartbeat_loop, a daemon
thread started at runner.py:2081, ticking every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 5s.
Verified live on a builder -- host clock 10:38:18Z against
runner_status.updated_at 10:38:16.599, two seconds old -- and it keeps
ticking through a build because it is a separate thread from the one blocked
in subprocess.run. Nothing in _dsynth_run needs touching.

It does not need dev-env exec either. The runner is root, so it can resolve
env_paths(env).writable / "work/dsynth/logs/..." and open the file directly:
a host-side read, no chroot spawn per tick. The offset-seeking reader for
exactly this is recoverable at commit 6275522; it was only ever wrong in the
TRACKER, where resolving the path needed root.

THE DESTINATION IS THE PROBLEM. The obvious cheap store -- a few columns on
runners or runner_status, overwritten in place, which the heartbeat is
already writing in the same transaction -- would be a TENTH direct sqlite
write from the runner, on precisely the channel poly-fij.4 exists to remove.
Storing it as artifacts instead is not an alternative: a tail's bytes differ
every tick, so nothing dedupes, and 480 ticks over a 40-minute build is
~15 MB per build and several GB across the jobs already run. A tail wants
one overwritten row, and the runner should not be writing rows.

So: heartbeat as the timer, and the tail rides the HTTP write channel
poly-fij.4 establishes -- most likely on the heartbeat endpoint itself,
since that is the one call already happening at the right cadence with the
right identity. That is option 3 of the three above, reached from the other
direction.

ALSO NOT FREE, and still unmeasured: a 32 KiB seek-read every 5s per running
build. If it matters the tail can tick on a multiple of the heartbeat
without changing anything else.

MEANWHILE, and independent of all of it: a failed dsynth_build row could
link to its bundle's logs/errors.txt (21,938 bytes on one measured job) and
logs/full.log.gz, which already exist and are already rendered by the
artifact viewer. That is one click from the row that failed instead of two
clicks and knowing where to look, it needs no runner change at all, and it
is most of the practical value. It does not solve liveness -- only a real
tail does.
DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-09-24. Was poly-fij.4 (auth); that was wrong. Auth is not on this bead's path: the five existing /v1 routes carry no credential, the runner already POSTs to them unauthenticated over loopback, and internet exposure is deferred. When poly-fij.4 lands it adds a header to the whole channel at once, the tail included.

The real blocker is poly-fij.12, and specifically only its first two steps. The note above says the tail should ride 'the heartbeat endpoint itself, since that is the one call already happening at the right cadence with the right identity' -- there is no such endpoint. /v1 has artifacts/get, artifacts/put, bundles/upsert, jobs/transition, user-context. Creating POST /v1/runners/heartbeat is poly-fij.12 step 2, and its own description calls that step 'self-contained -- proves the path end to end at trivial volume'.

So: poly-fij.12 steps 1-2 (the seam, then the heartbeat), then this. Steps 3-5 of that bead (activity_log batching, issues, the reads) are the rest of the epic and are NOT needed here.

poly-fij.7 is NOT on this path either, contrary to an earlier reading. The relay exists because the HOOKS only know 127.0.0.1. The tail's producer is the runner, which reaches the tracker directly.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: the renderer is already built and tested -- running_tailable_tool and attach_tool_tail in tracker/render/activity.py, four tests in test_render_tool_tail.py, both carrying 'Has no caller in production'. Only the wiring is missing. The offset reader is at commit 6275522. _dsynth_log_candidates (worker.py) resolves the path root-side.

ONE GAP MEASURED: the heartbeat can see _current_job_id and _current_stage (runner.py:292-293) but not env+origin, which the path resolver needs. Two more module globals, set where _current_stage is.
CODE READ 2026-09-24. THE FEATURE IS SMALLER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMES, and one part is bigger.

1. THE WHOLE VIEW LAYER SURVIVED poly-paee. Not just the two render helpers:
   _turn_cards.html         the tail block, tailbar, byte counts, log link
   progress.css:2633        .tool-tail / .tool-tailbar
   agentic-job.js:274       the 'last line N ago' ticker off data-mtime
   render/activity.py       running_tailable_tool + attach_tool_tail, 4 tests
poly-paee removed only the PRODUCER -- tracker/dsynth_tail.py, the route, and
the pages.py wiring. So this is a producer plus a sink plus re-attaching one
call, not a feature rebuild.

2. THE OFFSET READER IS REUSABLE VERBATIM, and it belongs on the runner now.
git show 6275522:dportsv3/tracker/dsynth_tail.py -- (path, offset) -> (text,
next offset, eof), nothing host-specific, delegating to
worker._dsynth_log_candidates. It was only ever wrong because it ran in the
TRACKER, which cannot resolve a dev-env path. On the runner, which is root,
it is correct as written. Moving it to dportsv3/agent/.

NO OFFSET TRACKING, though. Incremental reads would leave the row holding only
what arrived in the last tick -- zero lines on a quiet build. The page wants
the newest screenful every time, so the producer reads offset=-1,
max_lines=40 each tick and overwrites. That is a 32 KiB seek-read per tick,
still unmeasured, as this bead already flagged.

3. THE LIVE PATH IS THE PART THIS BEAD MISSED, and it is the same defect as
poly-qqx9.16 one surface over. In agentic_api.py the fragment computes
    window = activity_for_job(...) if rows else []
    cards  = group_activity_into_cards(window) if rows else []
and returns changed=bool(rows). A dsynth build writes NO activity_log rows for
40 minutes, so with the tail hung on a card the live view would never refresh
it -- exactly what the attempt strip's own comment says it fixed for itself:
'Gated on new rows it would sit frozen for the whole of a long build'.

Fixing it by ungating the card render would swap the whole card container every
3s for the length of a build, which recreates the tail's <pre> and so resets
the scroll position of the one element a reader may be scrolled inside. So the
tail gets ITS OWN SLOT, like strip_html and worktree_html: _tool_tail.html
extracted as a partial, sent as tail_html, swapped in place with the scroll
preserved.

THE SINK IS KEYED BY RUNNER, NOT BY JOB. One row per job would be unbounded
over time at up to 32 KiB each -- the artifact-growth objection this bead
already makes, just slower. Keyed by runner_id it is exactly N rows forever,
with job_id as a column: the page reads WHERE job_id = ? and correctly gets
nothing once that builder moved on, which is also the right semantics, since a
finished job's tail is superseded by logs/full.log.gz.

THE LOG LINK HAS NO TARGET WHILE RUNNING. The template's 'open the whole log'
href pointed at api_job_dsynth_tail, which poly-paee deleted, and full.log.gz
does not exist until the build ends. Guarded in the template rather than
rendered as an empty href.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24. Option 1 of the three, reached with poly-fij.12's carrier instead of a bespoke channel -- so the answer to 'or it goes' is that it stays.

  agent/dsynth_tail.py      the offset reader, moved from tracker/ unchanged.
                            It was never wrong -- only in the wrong process.
  runner._tail_target       what to tail, or None. Set at tool_start for a
                            TAILABLE tool, cleared when any call returns.
  runner._heartbeat_tail()  offset=-1, max_lines=40, never raises.
  presence.set_tail         one row per builder, overwritten; NULLs when
                            nothing runs; also blanked on deregister.
  runner_tail               new table, PK runner_id, job_id a column.
  job_tail(conn, job_id)    WHERE job_id = ? AND text IS NOT NULL.
  _tool_tail.html           the block extracted as a partial.
  tail_html                 its own slot, sent on EVERY poll.
  common/tools.py           TAILABLE_TOOLS declared once, both sides import.

4267 -> 4298 tests (31 new, two files).

MUTATION-CHECKED, the one that matters: gating the fragment's tail read on
 -- i.e. reintroducing the defect described above -- fails three tests
including test_the_tail_refreshes_with_no_new_activity_rows. Without that the
feature would have looked built and been frozen for the length of every build,
which is the exact failure mode this bead was filed to prevent.

FOUR THINGS THE REVIEW ADDED:
- Follow the newest line. A live tail whose <pre> is recreated every 3s renders
  scrolled to the TOP, showing the oldest of the last forty lines beside a
  label reading 'last line 4s ago'. It now pins to the bottom unless the reader
  has scrolled up.
- The swap runs AFTER the cards swap, since the slot lives inside the card
  stream and would otherwise be overwritten on any poll that had rows.
- deregister blanks the tail. The page's 'is a tool running' gate reads
  activity rows, and a stopped runner leaves those looking like a live build.
  A crash cannot run it; there the mtime ticker counting up is the tell.
- No 'open the whole log' link. It pointed at a route poly-paee deleted, and
  full.log.gz does not exist until the build ends -- href="" reads as broken.

COVERAGE: patch and convert both, since both run through PatchAttemptStep's
dispatcher. Triage has its own handler and nothing to tail -- it reads a log
that already exists rather than producing one.

STILL UNMEASURED, as this bead said: a 32 KiB seek-read every 5s per running
build. If it shows up, the tail can tick on a multiple of the heartbeat without
touching anything else -- _heartbeat_tail() is the only place that would change.

THE MEANWHILE ITEM IS NOT DONE and is now separable: a FAILED dsynth_build row
linking to its bundle's logs/errors.txt and logs/full.log.gz. That is about
finished builds, needs no runner change, and is worth its own bead.
CORRECTION to the note above: one word was lost to shell quoting. The mutation was "gating the fragment tail read on ROWS" -- that is, on new activity_log rows since the cursor, exactly as everything else in that fragment is gated.
title: Freeze: the dsynth tail needs the runner to publish it, or it goes

description:
Found on a live builder, 2026-09-24. The tracker must never run anything;
the runner may be remote (poly-fij), so anything that reaches into a build
environment is wrong by construction, not merely broken today.

TWO VIOLATIONS, both introduced by poly-qqx9 and the only two in the
package. There is no subprocess/Popen/os.system anywhere in
dportsv3/tracker/, and every other agent import is lifecycle (pure
constants) or fix_chat/llm (an outbound API call):

  tracker/worktree_source.py:52   from dportsv3.agent import worker
  tracker/dsynth_tail.py:133      from dportsv3.agent import worker

Both die as the unprivileged tracker account:

  from_workspace -> worker.emit_diff -> env_paths()
                 -> `dportsv3 dev-env path` -> require_root()   cli.py:282
                 -> _exec -> `dev-env exec`  -> require_root()   cli.py:811
  dsynth_tail.log_path -> worker._dsynth_log_candidates -> env_paths()

Verified on the host: the tracker service runs as `polytropos`, the runner
as root; chroot as non-root is EPERM; no sudoers grant for the tracker
user; no DPORTS_DEV_ENV_CMD in its rc.d script. from_workspace's bare
`except Exception` swallows all of it, so the working-tree band renders
nothing and the tail reports "no log" -- silently, on every job.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT CAUSE for the band being absent. The finished-job
fallback reads analysis/rescued/<job_id>.diff, which the rescue path
writes only when the harness RAISES. On the live builder:

  analysis/rescued/%    4 rows
  %changes.diff       289 rows

analysis/changes.diff is the canonical artifact every patch job writes
(runner._write_changes_diff). It was passed over because changes.diff is
per-BUNDLE and a retried bundle's copy may belong to a later job -- which
is true, and cost the band ~99% of the jobs it could have rendered.

SCOPE HERE: stop executing, and read artifacts only. Delete the worker
call in worktree_source; fall back to analysis/changes.diff, labelled,
since it may be a sibling job's; remove the tracker's live-tail wiring.

A running job then has no diff to show until the runner publishes one,
which is the follow-up -- and it must SAY that rather than render nothing.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. The tracker no longer runs anything.

worktree_source.from_workspace is DELETED, not repaired, and the module no
longer imports agent.worker. A test asserts the absence -- no
from_workspace attribute, no worker import, no subprocess in the file --
because the next person to want a live diff will reach for exactly this.

THE BAND NOW READS THE CANONICAL ARTIFACT. Order is rescued (per job,
exact) then analysis/changes.diff (per bundle, 289 on a live builder
against 4 rescued). The per-bundle one is LABELLED "from the bundle's
diff", with a title saying a retried bundle may share it between jobs --
the precision loss is stated rather than hidden, which is what made
preferring the exact artifact and showing nothing the wrong trade.

A PATCH JOB WITH NOTHING PUBLISHED SAYS SO: #worktree-pending, "no diff
published yet", and one line explaining the runner publishes when the
attempt ends. An absent band reads as "changed nothing". Only for type
patch -- on a triage or verify job it would be noise about work that job
never does.

THE TAIL WIRING IS GONE: tracker/dsynth_tail.py deleted, the
/api/jobs/<id>/dsynth-tail route deleted, and the read dropped from both
the job page and the live fragment. The reader is recoverable at commit
6275522 if poly-pvs2 takes the publish option.

render.running_tailable_tool and attach_tool_tail STAY, and say in their
own docstrings that they have no producer. They are pure, they are what any
publisher would feed, and the pairing they encode -- only a long tool gets
a tail, it hangs on the running row -- is the part worth not rediscovering.
Their tests moved to tests/test_render_tool_tail.py; the reader's 11 tests
went with the reader.

WHAT IS STILL NOT VISIBLE, and needs the runner: a RUNNING job's diff.
poly-5tgc. Until then a running patch job shows the pending note and a
finished one shows its diff, which is 289 jobs more than before.

4203 tests pass.
title: The tracker executes runner-side code, so the working tree and the dsynth tail are dead in deployment

description:
Found against a live builder's state.db, 2026-09-24.

activity_log is a GLOBAL rolling cap: runner.activity_log_max (default
5000), enforced by a DELETE in runner.py:1877. Observed on a live host:
one day of rows, ids 65074-70073, 5000 rows, and 3 DISTINCT JOBS out of
1,452 in the database (364 patch, 600 triage, 187 verify, 301 confirm).
A patch job spends roughly 1,600 rows, so the page holds about the last
three jobs.

Every surface poly-qqx9 added reads activity_log: the now-bar, the
attempt strip, the turn cards, the working-tree band. On an evicted job
they do not degrade, they assert -- a now-bar with nothing running, a
strip with no attempts, no turn cards at all, on a job that really did
run seven attempts. The old flat table had the same hole; the epic turned
one empty table into five positive claims.

The obligation is already assigned to this page. jobs.py:421 keeps
intra-job attempt detail OFF the occurrence aggregate for exactly this
reason: "a number that silently becomes 0 when it is evicted is worse
than no number. That detail stays on the job page, where the caveat is
local." No job-page template states it.

THE SIGNAL IS EXACT, so this needs no heuristic. jobs and job_events are
never pruned (jobs.py:415). A job whose job_events show that it ran,
which has no activity_log rows, and whose last transition predates
SELECT MIN(ts) FROM activity_log, has been pruned. One extra query.

Three states have to read differently, which is the whole bug:
pruned, nothing-yet (a job just claimed), and has-activity.

DEEPER QUESTION, DELIBERATELY NOT A BLOCKER: the cap is global, so one
chatty patch job (2,130 llm_turn rows in the observed window) evicts
every other job's history. Per-job retention, or simply a larger cap, is
a runner-side change with a disk cost. The page misreporting is a bug
whichever way that lands, so fix the page first.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-24. THE DESCRIPTION OVERSTATED THE SYMPTOM, and the real one is narrower and worse. The five surfaces do NOT assert: _attempt_strip.html guards on {% if strip and strip.attempts %}, _job_activity.html on {% if activity_cards %}, now_bar returns None without turns, and the working tree carries an `empty` flag. They all go quiet correctly. What asserted was one sentence, in the else branch nobody reads:
No activity recorded for this job.
False for every evicted job, and on a live builder that is 1,449 of 1,452. Said beside a durable transitions table showing seven attempts, which is what makes it read as a tracker fault rather than a retention policy. THREE STATES NOW READ DIFFERENTLY, which was the acceptance criterion: - pruned, nothing left -> "Activity has aged out", naming the cap, the oldest row the log still holds, when this job started, and that the lifecycle transitions are durable. - nothing yet -> the original sentence, unchanged. - partly pruned -> a note above the surviving cards. This is the worst case and was not in the original description: the survivors look like the whole story and the attempt strip counts only them. activity_pruning(conn, job_id) asks the two durable sources (jobs and job_events are never pruned) and FAILS CLOSED: with an empty activity_log there is no horizon, so it reports not-pruned rather than announcing pruning it cannot demonstrate. It says "any activity it recorded", never "its activity". Whether a job emitted activity at all is unknowable once the rows are gone, and a verify or confirm job may legitimately have emitted none -- the same uncertainty that made poly-qqx9.1's Q2 unanswerable. THE TRANSCRIPT ROUTE HAD THE SAME SENTENCE and now shares one partial, _activity_pruned.html, so the two wordings cannot drift. It is the surface that claims to be the WHOLE transcript, so the remnant note matters more there. One defect caught before it shipped: the transcript builds its template context AFTER its `with _conn()` block closes, so the query had to move inside the block rather than being a call in the dict. The global-vs-per-job cap question is untouched and still open -- see the description. The page is honest now whichever way that lands. 4209 tests pass; 8 new in tests/test_activity_pruning.py.
title: Job page presents a pruned activity log as a job where nothing happened

description:
Verified in code and reproduced against the real app, 2026-09-23.

POST /v1/artifacts/put-fs records any absolute path as an artifact: the
only check is Path(fs_path).is_file() (tracker/routes/ingest_api.py).
GET /v1/artifacts/get then reads that path and returns the bytes --
ArtifactStore.get_artifact returns ("fs", Path(row["fs_path"])) and the
route does file_path.read_bytes().

Two unauthenticated calls read any file the tracker account can read.
On a deployed host that account is exactly the one SECRET_MODES grants
delivery.token_file (0640) and llm.chat.api_key_file (0640), so one HTTP
request undoes the credential split those modes exist to make. The
comment on SECRET_MODES states the intent the split protects.
tracker.bind defaults to 0.0.0.0.

Neither route has a gate: forbid_anonymous appears 19 times across
tracker/routes/ and zero times in ingest_api.py, so
tracker.public_readonly does not cover this.

put_fs_ref also does ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, so an existing bundle's
artifact can be repointed. The diff an operator reads before Accept need
not be the diff on disk.

Nothing in the loop writes fs refs any more. hook_pkg_failure moved the
full log to put-blob because a recorded path is unresolvable from
another host and unresolvable in a chroot; the only remaining callers
are the artifact_store_client CLI subcommand and its own tests.

FIX: delete the write path -- the endpoint, ArtifactStore.put_fs_ref and
the CLI subcommand -- and confine the read path, so rows already written
into a deployed db cannot serve from outside the logs root either. The
read path has two resolvers that both trust fs_path today:
ArtifactStore.get_artifact for /v1, and render.resolve_artifact_path for
the browser routes (/api/bundles/{id}/artifacts/{relpath} and the
artifact viewer).

Confine to the logs root, not the evidence root: legitimate legacy rows
point at dsynth logs beside the evidence tree, not inside it.
notes:
FIXED 2026-09-23.

Write path gone: the /v1/artifacts/put-fs endpoint, ArtifactStore.put_fs_ref,
and the artifact_store_client put-fs subcommand. Nothing in the product can
write a backend='fs' row now, so no caller-controlled path can reach either
resolver.

Read path confined on /v1: get_artifact runs contained_fs_path(self.logs_root,
...) and returns None when the recorded path resolves outside it, so the route
404s. Containment is after realpath, so a symlink planted inside the tree does
not escape it. A legacy row naming a dsynth log still serves.

Verified by re-running the reproduction: put-fs 404, a row naming a credential
404 with an empty body, a row naming a log inside the logs root 200. 4198 tests
pass.

ONE HALF NOT DONE, filed as poly-szg2: render.resolve_artifact_path, which the
browser routes use, still serves fs_path as recorded. The same containment
fails 42 tests in five files whose fixtures write artifacts into tmp_path while
leaving paths.artifact_root at its production default -- the recorded path and
the configured root are unrelated there, so no boundary can hold until those
fixtures change. Not a live hole with the write path gone; the asymmetry is
recorded in a comment at both resolvers rather than left to be discovered.

THE BOUNDARY IS A JUDGEMENT, not a measurement. No real fs row was available to
read -- paths.artifact_root points at the builder host. The logs root is where
the old hook's dsynth log sat, but a deployed database may hold rows pointing
elsewhere, and those would now 404 on /v1. poly-szg2 carries the query to run
against a real state.db before the browser side picks the same boundary.
title: Unauthenticated arbitrary file read: put-fs records any path, /v1/artifacts/get serves it

close_reason:
Implemented. tool_loop emits tool_start at dispatch (attempt, turn, tool, call_id) and tool_call now carries the same call_id; PatchEventDispatcher writes a 'tool_start' activity row and keeps the event in trace_events. Tests: 3 dispatcher + 1 emitter (order is tool_start -> dispatch -> tool_call). Full suite 4065 passed.

ROW COST, as the bead asked: exactly one extra row per tool call, so patch and convert jobs grow activity_log by the tool-call share of their rows — roughly +50% on the shapes seen while designing, since tool rows and llm_turn rows run about 1:1. triage, verify and confirm are unaffected: they emit no tool calls at all (poly-qqx9.1). The exact multiplier needs the same live query the audit left open; poly-lvyr owns the global cap.

TWO NOTES FOR THE VIEW BEADS. The new stage is 'tool_start', which does NOT match the existing 'tool calls only' filter (stage LIKE 'tool:%') — deliberate, so the current filter keeps meaning completed calls; poly-qqx9.4 should decide whether the cards fold starts into the tool row. And the rows are visible on the job page NOW, before the cards land: a running tool reads as '<tool> started' in the table.
description:
A tool row reaches activity_log only when the tool RETURNS: steps.py:176
logs it from an event carrying ev.result and duration_ms. dsynth_build and
dsynth_test run 41 and 44 minutes on llvm19, so for forty minutes the page
adds nothing while the live badge keeps reading `live · just now` — the badge
reflects the poll (agentic-job.js, dpLive, 3s), not the job. A wedged runner
and a working one are indistinguishable for the most expensive operation the
loop performs.

Emit a start event at dispatch: tool name, its args, ts, and whatever pairs
it with the completion row so the end can match the start. Then the
completion row stays exactly as it is.

Three things in this epic depend on it and cannot be honestly built without
it: the now-bar's "what is running, for how long"; the attempt strip's phase
spans (today only end + duration_ms exist, so a bar chart would be inferring
its own left edges); and the in-row dsynth tail, which needs to know WHICH
log to tail, with which env and flavor, and when to stop.

Watch the cost: this doubles the row count for tool calls, and poly-lvyr is
already open on the activity_log global cap. Say in the close note what the
row-count increase measured out at.
notes:
NOTE (poly-qqx9.1, second pass): analysis/tool_trace.jsonl already holds
every event verbatim, written after the run. It does not replace this bead —
it lands when the run is over, and the whole point of the now-bar, the
attempt spans and the in-row tail is the job that is still going.
title: Emit tool_start, so a running tool is visible while it runs

close_reason: Audit complete on the source reading: field table, second-pass corrections, and the per-job-type matrix are on the bead. Findings pushed into poly-qqx9.3, .4, .6, .7, .9 and filed as poly-qqx9.12 and .13. Live confirmation against a builder state.db is three queries, listed on the bead; reopen if they contradict it.
description:
Before any of the view work: go field by field through specimen 06 and say,
for each, whether the tracker already holds it, can derive it, or does not
have it at all. Write the answer into this bead as a table. Every other child
of this epic is sized by that answer, which is why this one blocks them.

Three places where the answer is already known to be NO or MAYBE, found while
the design was being drawn — start here, then do the rest properly:

1. THE CARD'S SENTENCE HAS NO SOURCE. Each turn card leads with the model's
   own prose ("Hunk #2 rejected — the upstream file moved under the patch").
   The llm_turn activity row does not carry it: steps.py:199 logs a formatted
   token line and sets extra to the event minus 'type', which is counts plus
   tools_requested. _activity_row.html's `a.extra.text_only` branch confirms
   it — the page knows a turn was text-only, not what the text was. The prose
   lives in the session dump the artifact store holds, which
   agentic_session.html reads as turn cards already. So the card either joins
   activity to the session dump, or the dispatcher starts recording a short
   assistant summary per turn. DECIDE WHICH, and say why, before UI-shaping.

2. TOOL ARGS ARE PROSE, NOT FIELDS. The card renders `write_file
   Makefile.DragonFly.@2026Q3 · 118ms · +3 −1` — name, args and timing as
   separate cells. What is stored is one summary string per call from
   runner.py:3896 _summarize_tool_call(tool, args, result), whose own
   docstring says it is for an at-a-glance message column. extra_json carries
   attempt, turn, ok, and on failure rc/stderr_tail/stdout_tail — not the
   args. Either the dispatcher records args, or the card parses the summary,
   which is fragile and per-tool.

3. NOTHING RECORDS A TOOL STARTING. Confirmed at steps.py:176 — the row is
   written from the event carrying ev.result and duration_ms, i.e. on return.
   That is its own bead; note here what depends on it.

THE REST OF THE FIELD LIST, per band

  Now-bar: attempt n / runner.max_patch_attempts; turn number; the running
  tool and its start; elapsed; spend vs policy.tier_budgets[tier].max_tokens
  — and where the job's TIER is recorded, which the budget number needs.
  Attempt strip: per-attempt span boundaries per phase. attempt_start /
  attempt_end rows exist; whether phases inside an attempt can be bounded
  without tool_start is the question.
  Turn cards: turn id, verdict (derivable from the tools' ok flags?), tokens
  per turn (yes, extra_json), timestamp, tool rows per above.
  Working tree: file list with status letters, per-file +/-, which attempt
  each file arrived in, and the diff. worker.emit_diff(env, origin, relpath)
  returns the unified diff including untracked files, byte-capped — but it
  runs where the WORKSPACE is. Say how the tracker gets it, and whether
  per-attempt attribution exists anywhere or has to be recorded as it happens.
  Cost: per-turn and per-attempt exist (attempt_end carries billable_tokens
  and tokens, steps.py:53). Per-port across sibling jobs — does anything
  aggregate it?

ALL FIVE JOB TYPES. triage, patch, convert, verify and confirm share this
page and nothing branches on type. A field present only for patch jobs is a
finding, not a detail — say which bands degrade and to what.

Deliverable: the table, plus a one-line verdict per specimen-06 band —
buildable as drawn / buildable with a named runner change / needs a decision.
notes:
OPERATOR NOTES ARE A BAND TOO (poly-qqx9.11, added after this bead was
written). Audit them with the rest: there is no table for them today, so this
is a schema question rather than a 'is the field there' question. What one
needs: job_id, the text, who wrote it, created_ts, state (queued vs
delivered), and the turn it landed in — the delivered card is stamped with
that. Also say where the runner would read the queue from without a round
trip per turn.

poly-pf4a (the fix chat is not persisted) is the precedent not to repeat: a
note that exists only in one browser is worse than no note, because the
transcript then cannot explain why the agent changed course.
AUDIT, first pass (2026-09-23). Read: tool_loop.py, attempt_loop.py,
triage.py, steps.py, session_dump.py, settings.py, schema.py,
worker.py, render/activity.py, agentic_queries/*.

HEADLINE: THE CARD'S SENTENCE DOES NOT EXIST IN A DEFAULT DEPLOYMENT.
The llm_turn event (tool_loop.py:338) carries prompt/completion/total/
cached/billable, cumulative_*, tools_requested and text_only — never the
assistant text. The text survives only in the session dump, and
runner.dump_session (settings.py:327) defaults to FALSE and is described as
a debug switch ("Large, and the single most useful thing to have when an
attempt goes wrong"). So on a normal builder there is nothing to render.

TWO THINGS ARE BETTER THAN FEARED
  - tool_call (tool_loop.py:450) DOES carry args in full, plus the whole
    result dict and duration_ms. PatchEventDispatcher (steps.py:152) throws
    the args away and stores _summarize_tool_call's one-liner
    (runner.py:3896). The args are dropped, not missing.
  - attempt_start (attempt_loop.py:512) carries its own `budget`, so the
    now-bar's denominator needs no tier lookup and no settings read.

FIELD TABLE   (present | derivable | MISSING)

  NOW-BAR
    attempt n, turn ................ present   extra.attempt / extra.turn
    max attempts ................... derivable runner.max_patch_attempts at
                                               read time; not stored per job
    running tool + args + started .. MISSING   row is written on return
                                               (steps.py:176)
    elapsed ........................ MISSING   same cause
    spend .......................... present   cumulative_billable_tokens
    budget ......................... present   attempt_start.budget

  ATTEMPT STRIP
    boundaries ..................... present   attempt_start / attempt_end
    outcome ........................ present   attempt_end.rebuild_ok
    per-attempt tokens ............. present   attempt_end.billable_tokens
                                               (render/activity.py already
                                               folds all three)
    phase spans within an attempt .. MISSING   only end ts + duration_ms

  TURN CARDS
    id, ts, tokens ................. present
    verdict ........................ derivable tool extra.ok, rebuild_ok
    the model's sentence ........... MISSING   see HEADLINE
    tool name ...................... present   stage = 'tool:<name>'
    tool args as fields ............ DROPPED   in the event, not in the row
    duration, ok, rc, diagnostics .. present   extra (tails capped 2000)

  WORKING TREE
    the diff ....................... derivable worker.emit_diff(env, origin,
                                               relpath); _current_diff
                                               already calls it per retry and
                                               gives it to the MODEL only
    the env to call it with ........ MISSING   no env column on jobs; only
                                               verify_requests.env
    per-attempt attribution ........ MISSING   nothing records which attempt
                                               first touched a file
    job -> occurrence .............. present   jobs.bundle_id (patch/verify
                                               set it; triage sets
                                               bundle_dir — tests/
                                               test_jobs_bundle_id_fk.py)

  IN-ROW TAIL
    path ........................... present   env_paths(env).writable/work/
                                               dsynth/logs/<stem>[@flavor].log
    flavor ......................... present   jobs.flavor
    env ............................ MISSING   as above
    byte cap ....................... present   worker.dsynth_log

  OPERATOR NOTES ................... NOTHING   no table, no route

  COST
    per turn / attempt / job ....... present
    per port across sibling jobs ... MISSING   list_port_bundles carries no
                                               spend

DEGRADATION ACROSS JOB TYPES. attempt_start/attempt_end come from
attempt_loop, i.e. patch-shaped work. triage.py:132 emits llm_turn as well,
so a triage job has turns but no attempts; the strip and the attempt
grouping collapse to one implicit group for triage/verify/confirm. Design
that deliberately rather than discovering it.

VERDICT PER BAND
  now-bar ......... needs tool_start; everything else is there
  attempt strip ... needs tool_start for honest spans
  turn cards ...... buildable minus the prose, which needs a decision
  working tree .... needs env, and a decision on attribution
  in-row tail ..... needs env; local-only until poly-fij.7
  operator notes .. needs a table
  cost ............ buildable; per-port wants a small aggregate
AUDIT, second pass — three corrections to the table above and two
simplifications. Read: steps.py rescue path, runner.py _write_tool_trace,
env_resolver.py, render/sessions.py.

MISSED

1. analysis/tool_trace.jsonl ALREADY HOLDS EVERY EVENT VERBATIM.
   PatchEventDispatcher appends each event to trace_events (steps.py:108)
   and the runner persists them as JSONL (runner.py:4006), written in the
   rescue path (steps.py:841) so it survives however the run ended. Its own
   docstring: "its put_file arguments alone let a human reconstruct the
   edits". render/sessions.py already loads it and indexes llm_turn events
   into a turn->tokens map for the session viewer.
   So ARGS ARE NOT LOST — they are unavailable LIVE (the file is written
   after the run) and not queryable per row. That weakens the "stop dropping
   args" case from data loss to live availability, which is still the case
   the job page needs, but it is a smaller claim.

2. THE TERMINAL-JOB WORKING TREE NEEDS NOTHING NEW. The same rescue path
   writes analysis/changes.diff — whole tree vs the bundle base with the
   --intent-to-add bracket, so never-committed files surface as additions —
   and analysis/rescued/<job_id>.diff, the same bytes at a path no later job
   overwrites. Both are written when non-empty even when the attempt failed.
   So the band can be phased: terminal jobs render from the rescued diff,
   which is already per-job and already durable; only a RUNNING job needs
   emit_diff and therefore the env.

3. WHY THE ENV IS ABSENT, precisely. env_resolver's top precedence is
   `job.dev_env` — but that lives in the queue FILE, written as a
   `dev_env=` line (runner.py:2840), not in the DB. get_job is
   `SELECT * FROM jobs`, so the tracker never sees it. The column finding
   stands; it is one column written at claim time, not a new subsystem.

OVER-COMPLICATED — DROPPED

4. Per-attempt file attribution does not need its own bead or its own
   storage. Once a write tool's args are on the row, attribution is a query:
   the first attempt whose write-tool row names that path. attempt_loop.py:109
   already defines _WRITE_TOOLS for exactly this set. Fold it into the
   working-tree bead.

5. THE PROSE IS NOT A BLOCKER. A card without it still carries turn id,
   verdict, tokens, duration and its tool rows — already far past the table
   it replaces. Do not enable runner.dump_session for this: it is large by
   its own description, and its artifacts land per attempt, so they are not
   live within the attempt anyway. Treat a capped (~300 char) assistant
   summary on the llm_turn event as an ENHANCEMENT, and make the card
   degrade cleanly when it is absent — which it must do regardless, for
   every job that already ran.

NET EFFECT ON THE PLAN
  keystone ....... tool_start (poly-qqx9.2), unchanged
  new, small ..... dev_env on the jobs row, written at claim time
  new, small ..... tool args (+ optional capped assistant summary) into the
                   activity row's extra_json — a change inside
                   PatchEventDispatcher, no new event
  poly-qqx9.7 .... phase it: terminal from rescued/<job_id>.diff first
                   (zero new data), live from emit_diff second
  poly-qqx9.9 .... add the per-port aggregate
  dropped ........ a separate attribution bead; enabling dump_session
AUDIT, third pass — the per-job-type answer, which is the one that shapes
the cards. Read: triage.py, steps.py (_triage_event, PatchEventDispatcher,
both construction sites), verify_fix.py, runner.py activity stages.

WHAT EACH JOB TYPE ACTUALLY WRITES

  patch    attempt_start / attempt_end, llm_turn (attempt+turn), tool:<name>,
           decision, attempt_workspace_reset, observations_masked.
           Everything the design draws.
  convert  the same — steps.py:1445 builds a second PatchEventDispatcher for
           that flow, so it behaves like patch.
  triage   llm_turn ONLY, through _triage_event (steps.py:358), which returns
           early on every other event type. Its extra carries phase="triage",
           turn, snippet_round and the token fields — and NO `attempt` key.
           No tool rows. No attempts.
  verify   nothing of the kind. No on_event anywhere in verify_fix.py; the
           job's activity is flat operational stages written by the runner:
           verify_branch_checkout, verify_complete, verify_failed,
           verify_branch_dropped, ...
  confirm  same shape as verify — a build, not an agent loop.

CONSEQUENCES, and they are design consequences rather than details

  - The turn card is a PATCH/CONVERT shape. A triage job renders cards with
    no tool rows and no attempt grouping (group_activity_by_attempt puts
    attempt-less rows in a "setup" group, which is already the right
    behaviour). A verify or confirm job has no turns AT ALL — the cards
    band must render its operational stages instead, or say plainly that
    this job type has none. Decide that in poly-qqx9.4; do not let it be
    discovered by whoever opens a confirm job first.
  - The attempt strip (poly-qqx9.6) exists only for patch and convert. For
    the other three it should be absent, not empty.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FIRST-PASS TABLE

  - MAX ATTEMPTS IS STORED, not only a setting. attempt_start carries
    `iterations` and the dispatcher persists the whole event
    (steps.py:139: extra = every field but type). So "attempt 3 of N" reads
    N from the row that opened the attempt — the value the run actually
    used — rather than from runner.max_patch_attempts at render time, which
    would misreport any job that ran under a different setting.
  - `ok` IS ALWAYS PRESENT as a key on a tool row, including as None:
    steps.py:154 sets it unconditionally from the result dict. The card's
    verdict logic can rely on the key existing and must treat None as
    "no verdict", not as failure.

STILL UNVERIFIED AGAINST LIVE DATA

  Everything above is read from source. It should be confirmed once against
  a real builder's state.db — it is three queries, not an investigation:

    SELECT stage, COUNT(*) FROM activity_log GROUP BY stage;
    SELECT j.type, a.stage, COUNT(*) FROM activity_log a
      JOIN jobs j USING (job_id) GROUP BY j.type, a.stage;
    SELECT extra_json FROM activity_log WHERE stage='attempt_start' LIMIT 3;

  This bead is closed on the source reading, which is what the view beads

title: Data audit: does the tracker hold every field the job-detail design renders?

description:
The job detail page renders every kind of runner work — triage, patch,
convert, verify, confirm — as one reverse-chronological table inside a 75vh
scroller. Nothing in it branches on job.type; the only fork is live vs
terminal, and the terminal branch is the better one. An operator arrives with
five questions and the page answers none of them:

  Q1 which attempt am I on
  Q2 what is it doing right now
  Q3 what has this cost
  Q4 what has it changed
  Q5 how do I tell it something

Measured on the page as it stands: the header says `patching` and nothing
else; the only "attempt" shown is `Recent attempts 0/3 failures in last 2h`,
which is the port budget over a time window, not this job's attempt; a tool
row is written only when the tool RETURNS (steps.py:176 logs it with
ev.result and duration_ms), so a 41-minute dsynth build writes nothing for 41
minutes while the badge reads `live · just now` because it reflects the poll;
the page never shows a diff and never links to its own occurrence, though
jobs.bundle_id exists and attempt_loop._current_diff() hands the carried
overlay diff to the MODEL at every retry; and the only control is
`Abandon job (mark dead)`.

DESIGN SOURCE

  Artifact "Five Ways to Watch a Job",
  https://claude.ai/artifact/9CK76aSHpv8oF36GZUrXwV, version 9, read
  2026-09-23. Seven specimens; SPECIMEN 06 ("One page, all five") is the
  target and the thing to compare against. SPECIMEN 07 records the placement
  decision that produced it. Re-read before starting; if the artifact has
  moved on, correct these children rather than working from this text.

  The specimens are driven by schema-shaped SAMPLE data. Field names and
  vocabularies are the tracker's; the numbers are invented. Two in
  particular must NOT be copied: attempt "3 of 4" (the real denominator is
  runner.max_patch_attempts, default 3) and the "400,000" token budget (the
  real one is policy.tier_budgets[<tier>].max_tokens — AUTO 30k, ASSIST
  120k, CONVERT 150k, MANUAL never runs the agent).

THE SHAPE, as 06 settles it

  1. Pinned now-bar — attempt n of max, turn, the tool running now with a
     ticking elapsed, spend against the tier budget.
  2. Attempt strip — one track per attempt, segmented by what consumed the
     wall clock. The shape of a patch job is two dsynth builds and a
     rounding error of thinking, and a table cannot show that.
  3. Turn cards, full width — one per model turn, verdict carried by a
     glyph (passed / tool failed / running / attempt boundary), tool calls
     nested inside with their args, elapsed and outcome, diagnostics folded
     under the call that produced them and open by default when they failed.
     Last 5 only; the whole transcript is one click away.
  4. Working tree band, full width — files changed with per-attempt
     attribution and the diff beside them.
  5. No separate tail pane: a build's output belongs to the tool row running
     it, and goes away with it.

  Placement of the tree was decided in specimen 07 against three
  alternatives (sticky rail, inline-only, drawer). Band below won: the diff
  gets full width, and the rail's permanent ~330px tax buys something you
  look at intermittently. If that is revisited, 07 is where the argument is.

  6. A composer at the foot: an operator note joins the transcript as its own
     card and is delivered ON THE NEXT TURN — the moment the running tool
     returns — not at the attempt boundary. Specimen 06 shows both states, a
     queued note and a delivered one; the delivered one is placed where it
     explains the turn that followed it.

  Q5 is the only item that changes what the agent DOES rather than what an
  operator can see, so it carries the most runner risk in this epic. It was
  added to 06 deliberately after the rest was settled (version 9 of the
  artifact); specimen 05 is the wider exploration, including the pause and
  approval-gate variants, which are NOT in scope here.

WHY A NEW EPIC AND NOT poly-x3pg

  poly-x3pg exists to make the built views match the operations console mock.
  That mock's own job detail (pipelineJobDetail) is an activity TABLE with a
  facts rail — this work deliberately replaces it. Filing it under x3pg would
  make that epic unclosable and blur which source measures what. Instead one
  child here ports the agreed design INTO the console mock, so the console
  keeps a single authoritative source afterwards.

CLOSING REQUIREMENT (poly-ez41)

  Render specimen 06 and the built page at the same width, side by side, and
  look at them. Every surviving divergence is a decision and gets written
  down in the child that made it, with its measurement or its reason.
notes:
DESIGN SOURCE, SETTLED (poly-qqx9.10, 2026-09-23)

Artifact "Polytropos Operations Console",
https://claude.ai/artifact/6UXFSQDntZKwsrwC1rLjgM, VERSION 11, published
2026-09-23. pipelineJobDetail is now this epic's design, ported from
specimen 06 into the console's own vocabulary. That page is the one
authoritative source for the job-detail surface from here on, and it is
what poly-x3pg should measure the built page against.

The intermediate remains readable and is no longer the reference:
artifact "Five Ways to Watch a Job",
https://claude.ai/artifact/9CK76aSHpv8oF36GZUrXwV, version 9, read
2026-09-23. Specimen 06 is the layout the port carries; specimen 07
records the placement decision behind it.

Two sources for one surface is the state this settles. The warning above
about the specimens' invented numbers still applies to anyone reading
them: the port uses the console's own sample instead (attempt 3 of 3,
264,110 of 400,000, the figures ACTIVITY already records for j-10442).

SIDE-BY-SIDE, DONE (2026-09-23)

Both surfaces rendered at 1500px in headless Chrome and put in two
columns: the design (console mock v11, pipelineJobDetail) beside the
built page (/agentic/jobs/pj-af31c2 on a seeded db with a running
dsynth, a failed tool, a queued operator note and a rescued diff).

THEY READ AS THE SAME APPLICATION. Same order, same vocabulary, same
colours: pinned now-bar; attempt strip with per-attempt billable beside
each track; turn cards newest-first with the queued note pinned above
them; the build's tail inside the running tool row with "last line N
ago"; the working-tree band; the composer; the facts and token panels;
the flat table collapsed under them.

THE COMPARISON FOUND A REAL DEFECT, which is what it is for. The built
page's working-tree band was ABSENT: a live emit_diff read that returns
an ok result whose body is not a diff counted as "the live read worked",
so the rescued artifact behind it was never reached and the band hid
itself on a job that had changes recorded. from_workspace now requires
the body to contain "diff --git " before it counts. Fixed and tested.

TWO DIVERGENCES SURVIVE. Both are decisions, not accidents:

1. ORDER. The built page keeps the summary card and the lifecycle-
   transitions table between the attempt strip and the turn cards -- on
   the seeded job that is ~600px of chrome between "where is it" and
   "what is it doing". The design puts the facts in a panel at the foot
   and has no transitions table at all. The facts and the transitions
   are real records that predate this epic and nothing here asked to
   move them, so they stayed. Filed as poly-qqx9.14 rather than changed
   under cover of this epic.

2. THE FACTS ARE COLLAPSED. The built page's Token usage and Prior
   attempts are section-collapse disclosures at the foot; the design
   has Job + Token cost always open beside the composer. Deliberate:
   those two sections predate this epic in that form, the billable
   figure an operator needs at a glance is already in the now-bar, and
   the largest turn is named in the collapsed summary line (poly-qqx9.9)
   so the card's headline reads without opening it.
